quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: You must use your low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off wet surfaces and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop Sign Ahead.
Side Road.
Railroad Warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop Sign Ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: Blue traffic signs give information about:

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance.
Mileage information, such as distances to specific locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs provide information about motorist services like rest areas, food, gas, and hospitals.

questions.question: When is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles
Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing
Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, curves, or hills where you cannot see ahead. Only pass where signs and pavement markings allow it. Always make sure you have enough space to pass safely.

questions.question: This sign tells a driver that:

options.text: A construction flagger is ahead.
A police officer is ahead.
A parking attendant is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A construction flagger is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Always follow their directions. Flaggers wear orange, yellow, or bright jackets and use paddles and flags to direct traffic through work zones.

questions.question: If your vehicle is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, and steer in the direction the rear is sliding. If you have anti-lock brakes, apply them firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: When following a truck at night, you should dim your headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Always dim your headlights when following a truck at night. Bright lights reflect off the truck's large mirrors and blind the driver.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, you should:

options.text: Look toward the center of the roadway.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. This lets you see enough to stay on course. Do not retaliate by keeping your own high beams on.

questions.question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see, you should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Make constant visual checks.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make constant visual checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss in blind spots. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
Stop if you are driving in the same direction.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, regardless of your direction of travel.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: What effect does a blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent have?

options.text: It will not affect your driving.
It will not put other drivers at risk.
It will double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: Which statement describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They trust that other drivers will do the right thing.
They predict what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no help and give none to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They predict what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to avoid them.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Stop completely, check for traffic, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: How do you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with its siren and lights on, drive to the right edge and stop. Try not to stop in the intersection. You can go again after it passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A 35 mph speed zone starts after the curve.
Do not drive slower than 35 mph on the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less for the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less for the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to hazards ahead. Speed advisory signs show the safe speed for the road condition. Slow down to the recommended speed.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to keep your spot.
Stay in your position no matter what.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, let merging vehicles enter your lane.

questions.question: Is it legal to use a hands-free phone while driving if you are 19 or older?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Illinois law bans handheld phones and texting while driving. Drivers 19 and older can use hands-free devices or Bluetooth technology.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and stop if other cars are coming.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Go through carefully without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Stop at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see oncoming traffic. Only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake and hold it down.
Hold the steering wheel tight and brake gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and brake gently.
questions.explanation: When a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and braking lightly. Do not stop on the road. Move to a safe place off the road.

questions.question: The best way to avoid danger while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening all around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Keep your eyes focused straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening all around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always watch what is happening around your vehicle. Check the front, sides, and rear regularly. This helps you see problems early and change speed or position safely.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because a lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, signs warn you about workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn allowed.
No U-turn allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and illegal to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a crosswalk ahead, marked or unmarked. Watch for pedestrians and let them cross safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Cars on the right go first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let other traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: At this sign, slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians pass. Stop if needed before continuing.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a gap large enough to match traffic speed.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough to match traffic speed.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to get your vehicle up to the speed of other cars.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road crosses ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road crosses ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to situations they may not see right away. This sign warns of a side road intersection ahead.

questions.question: If you see a blind person with a guide dog or white cane:

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must yield to them.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to them.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind people carry a white cane or use a guide dog. You must always yield to a person with a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangular sign with black letters means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads where passing is not allowed.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer distances to stop and cause more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the penalty for illegally passing a stopped school bus?

options.text: Suspension of driving privileges or vehicle registration, plus a $300 fine.
A 60-day suspension of driving privileges.
A $30 fine and 14-day suspension of driving privileges.

questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension of driving privileges or vehicle registration, plus a $300 fine.
questions.explanation: Passing a stopped school bus with flashing lights results in suspension of your driver's license, a mandatory $300 fine, and community service ordered by the court. If you were not the driver, the vehicle owner must give the State's Attorney the driver's name, or the vehicle registration will be suspended for three months.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
No right turns permitted.
Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns permitted.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. You cannot turn right at an intersection with this sign.
